note.p: See Ed Pope: A and J Black booksellers 7 Leadenhall-st from 1800 to 1822 trading as Black, Kingsbury and Parry from 1807 to 1812 (bbti). We have coded Black uder this identity only to 1822. We think it is likely he continued in business but, while early entries are connected to the viscinity of other booksellerss, this is more difficult to establish for later entries.

Some of the 'Black' entries are likely to have been John Black (1783-1855), ODNB a translator, Greek scholar, and eventually editor of the Morning Chronicle. Acccording to the ODNB he moved to London only in 1810 but it is unclear if that was his first visit, or how much confidence we should place on that date. It is very likely that he appeared in Godwin's networks at some point. But he is not identified distinctly from the 1809 Black.
We have coded all black's under this identity - while emphasising that we cannot be certain whether there arre in fact two Blacks involved, only one, or several.
